text:
Stockton University president discusses higher education challenges and partnerships
A. M. Egan
Joe Bertolino, Ed.D., president of Stockton University, discussed the current challenges facing higher education and the importance of strategic partnerships in supporting the long-term success of colleges and universities during a conversation with Steve Adubato on Aug. 19.
Bertolino addressed several issues impacting institutions today, focusing on how collaboration can help colleges adapt to changing demands. He said that working with partners inside and outside academia is key to overcoming obstacles and ensuring future viability for universities.
"Strategic partnerships are essential for colleges and universities to thrive in today's environment," Bertolino said during the discussion. He highlighted that these collaborations can provide new opportunities for students, faculty, and staff while strengthening institutional resilience.
The conversation also touched on broader efforts by organizations such as the New Jersey Business and Industry Association to facilitate cooperation among businesses, government entities, and academic institutions. The association serves as the nation's largest statewide employer group representing private-sector employers throughout New Jersey; it offers advocacy, practical information, cost-saving benefits, and advances competitive excellence for its members, according to the official website.
Michele Siekerka serves as president and chief executive officer of this organization, according to its official website.
Bertolino concluded by reiterating his commitment to fostering strong relationships across sectors: "It is through these partnerships that we can address both immediate challenges in higher education as well as prepare for long-term success."
